rules.title: No C++-style class/new/delete
rules.statement: The language has no `class` declaration, `new` expression, or `delete` statement. Heap allocation is expressed via `Box` (and other library owning types), not a built-in `new`/`delete` pair.
rules.divergence: Logos addition/removal vs C++; Rust-conformant (Rust also has no class/new/delete).

rules.title: Chained comparisons rejected
rules.statement: A comparison chain with 2+ comparators in a row (`a < b < c`) is rejected at sema with the diagnostic "chained comparisons not supported; use `a < b && b < c`". It parses (CHAINED_CMP) but is not a valid program.

rules.title: Parenthesized type is structurally its inner type
rules.statement: A parenthesized type `(T)` is unwrapped to its inner type `T`; `(T)` and `T` are structurally identical.

rules.title: Double reference types desugar to nested references
rules.statement: `&&T` resolves to a nested reference `&(&T)`; `&&mut T` resolves to `&(&mut T)`.

rules.title: Unsized slice [T] cannot appear by value
rules.statement: The bare unsized slice type `[T]` (Kind::UnsizedSlice) may not appear by value; it is only legal behind `&`/`*const`/`*mut` (canonicalised to a sized Slice) or as a `T: ?Sized` substitution.

rules.title: Tail expression is implicit return
rules.statement: A trailing expression with no terminating `;` at statement position synthesizes an implicit `return expr` for a non-void function.

rules.title: Byte-string literal is [u8; N]
rules.statement: A byte-string literal `b"..."` at expression position lowers to an array literal of type `[u8; N]` (escapes decoded).

rules.title: Char literal is a Unicode scalar
rules.statement: A char literal `'X'` denotes a single Unicode scalar value, decoded to a `u32` scalar.

rules.title: Expression-as-callee invocation
rules.statement: `(expr)(args)` invokes the value produced by `expr` as a callee, routed through closure-call or fn-ptr-call.

rules.title: break/continue/return usable in expression position
rules.statement: `break`, `continue`, and `return` may appear in expression position (Never-typed); the bare `return` form carries no value. They type-check as `!`/Never so surrounding expressions accept them.

rules.title: Nested function lifted to a free function
rules.statement: A `fn name(params) [-> T] { body }` at statement position is lifted to a top-level free function (gensym name); the local name is bound as a fn-ptr `let`. A nested fn does not capture enclosing locals.

rules.title: Union layout and unsafe field access
rules.statement: A `union NAME { f: T, ... }` is a struct-shaped type whose size is max-of-fields aligned to max field alignment; reading or writing a union field requires an `unsafe` block.

rules.title: static items have global storage; mut access is unsafe
rules.statement: `static [mut] NAME: T = expr;` is a true global with a stable address and `&STATIC` identity. Reads and writes of a `static mut` require `unsafe`. A static with no initializer is an extern (external-linkage) declaration.

rules.title: offset_of! yields compile-time field offset
rules.statement: `offset_of!(Type, field)` evaluates at compile time to the byte offset of `field` within `Type`'s ABI layout, as an i64 constant.

rules.title: sizeof...(T) yields pack length
rules.statement: `sizeof...(T)` is a value-position expression yielding the length of the type pack `T` as a `u64`.

rules.title: Float-literal patterns rejected
rules.statement: A float-literal pattern parses but is rejected at sema (not a valid match pattern).

rules.title: String-literal pattern lowers to equality guard
rules.statement: A string-literal pattern `match s { "foo" => ... }` is matched by lowering to a `str_eq` guard.

rules.title: let with complex pattern checked for refutability
rules.statement: `let <pattern> = expr;` for a pattern beyond a simple ident/tuple is an irrefutable destructure: sema checks the pattern is irrefutable and lowers it via `match`.

rules.title: Destructuring assignment into existing places
rules.statement: Destructuring assignment `(a,b)=e` / `[a,b]=e` / `S{a,b}=e` writes into EXISTING places (not new bindings), desugared to `let tmp = rhs;` followed by per-place assignments.

rules.title: if-let chain falls to else on any segment failure
rules.statement: `if let P1 = e1 && let P2 = e2 && cond { THEN } else { ELSE }` evaluates a flat sequence of refutable binds and boolean conditions left-to-right; any failed bind or false condition takes the ELSE branch.

rules.title: extern block applies its ABI as a default
rules.statement: `extern "ABI" { extern_fn* }` splices its function items into the module item stream; the block ABI applies as a default to children that do not specify their own ABI. An omitted block ABI is the default Logos-internal ABI.

rules.title: use {..} disambiguated by first-character case
rules.statement: In `use pkg.Path.X.{V1, V2, ...};` the last dotted segment `X` disambiguates by its first character's case: uppercase ⇒ enum-variant bare-name shorthand import; lowercase ⇒ grouped sub-package import.

rules.title: Inner attribute applies at file/module level
rules.statement: `#![name]` / `#![name(args)]` / `#![name=val]` is a file/module-level inner attribute, distinct from per-item `#[...]` attributes.

rules.title: metacall executes a call at compile time
rules.statement: `metacall <call_expr>` executes the wrapped call at compile time; at module-item position the JIT'd callee returns an item blob whose emitted items are spliced into the module.

rules.title: quote_* produce typed AST/Type literals
rules.statement: `quote_item! { item* }`, `quote_expr! { expr }`, and `quote_ty! { type }` are typed literals yielding item-list, expression, and Type AST values respectively. Antiquotation `$ident` (a Type-valued binding) and `$ident...` (an Array<Type> binding) are legal only inside `quote_ty!`.

rules.title: Function-style macros resolve to #[fn_macro] fns
rules.statement: `name!(args)` / `name![args]` resolves CALLEE against `#[fn_macro]` functions with argument ASTs passed as expression blobs; `name!{...}` at item position routes through item-splice (callee returns an item list).

rules.title: Doc comments attach as documentation
rules.statement: Outer doc comments (`///`, `/** */`) accumulate and attach to the next item; inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*! */`) accumulate into the module-level inner documentation. The comment markers are stripped.
